title: Battle of Marathon
description: Added from the Generations curriculum import (Preparing the World for Jesus (1st ed., 2020)). Dated only by the Generations books cited below; no tier 1–4 chronology covers this event.

chronologies.date: “For in the three following generations of Darius the son of Hystaspes, Xerxes the son of Darius, and Artaxerxes the son of Xerxes, more woes befell Greece than in the twenty generations preceding Darius”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 6.98 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 408 (PDF p. 410)
chronologies.note: Said of the Delos earthquake as Datis's fleet sailed for Eretria and Marathon. Herodotus counts the Persian kings to Artaxerxes, son of Xerxes.

chronologies.date: “It was then the ninth day of the first decade; and they could not march out of Sparta on the ninth, when the moon had not reached the full”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 6.106 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 411 (PDF p. 413)
chronologies.note: The Spartans wait for the full moon before marching: a day of the month, not a year. DERIVED (not Herodotus's figure): About 490 BC for the battle, counted back from CFAH AP-13 (480 BC) with Herodotus's intervals in 7.1–7.37 (see 7.1). Consistent with Generations 490 BC (provisional).

chronologies.date: “After the full of the moon two thousand Lacedaemonians came to Athens”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 6.120 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 417 (PDF p. 419)
chronologies.note: They marched from Sparta in three days but arrived after the battle.

chronologies.date: “all Asia was in commotion by the space of three years”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 7.1 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 426 (PDF p. 428)
chronologies.note: Darius prepares a second expedition after the news of Marathon. DERIVED (not Herodotus's figure): About 490 BC for Marathon. Chain from CFAH AP-13 (Xerxes invades Greece, 480 BC): the host wintered at Sardis and marched "on the first approach of spring" (7.37), having set out "at the close of the fifth year" from the recovery of Egypt (7.20), so Egypt was recovered about 485/484 BC; that was "the year following the death of Darius" (7.7), so Darius died about 486/485 BC; he died "in the year following the revolt of Egypt" (7.4), about 487/486 BC, and the revolt came "in the fourth year" after the news of Marathon (7.1), so Marathon was about 490 BC (±1). Consistent with Generations 490 BC (provisional).
